comparison: Perfect agreement on DKK3 elevation in AD (C2, C3, C25-C34). Both evaluations find the evidence strongly supported across multiple datasets (RNAseq, Western blots, proteomics). OpenEval provides detailed statistical assessment while peer reviewers emphasize the importance of early disease changes.

Complete agreement on DKK3 localization and accumulation in AD mouse models (C4, C5, C40-C51). Both evaluations accept the Western blot and confocal microscopy data showing extracellular DKK3 increases and neuritic accumulation around plaques without concerns.

Strong agreement on NMDAR-mediated regulation of DKK3 secretion (C53, C54, C56-C58, C60). Peer reviewers acknowledge the mechanistic finding without criticism. OpenEval notes a borderline statistical result (p=0.0726) requiring alternative testing, but both find overall evidence supported. OpenEval addresses C52 and C55 not mentioned in peer review.

Full agreement on bidirectional synaptic effects of DKK3 (C61-C70). Both evaluations accept the gain/loss of function data showing effects on excitatory and inhibitory synapses. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as supporting main conclusions; OpenEval notes adequate controls but mentions some statistical details are not fully specified.

Complete agreement on GSK3-mediated pathway for excitatory synapse effects (C71-C77, C84). Both evaluations accept the pharmacological rescue experiments. OpenEval notes the inference assumes no parallel pathways contribute, while peer reviewers emphasize this advances understanding of Wnt pathway mechanisms in AD.

Full agreement on pathway segregation with JNK mediating inhibitory synapse effects (C78-C83, C85). Both evaluations accept the distinct downstream pathways. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of bidirectional pharmacology; peer reviewers acknowledge this as part of the dual signaling mechanism.

Complete agreement on differential requirements for endogenous DKK3 (C86-C92). Both evaluations accept the loss-of-function data showing asymmetric effects on synapse types. OpenEval notes the mEPSC amplitude reduction complicates interpretation slightly; peer reviewers accept this as part of gain/loss of function studies.

Strong agreement on therapeutic rescue of synaptic defects (C93-C100, C104). Both evaluations affirm DKK3 knockdown restores synapse numbers in AD models. OpenEval addresses C101-C103 (DKK1 independence) which peer reviewers cover separately in R12. All reviewers emphasize this as compelling evidence.

Both address DKK1 independence (C101-C103). OpenEval includes this within the therapeutic rescue evaluation (R8), while peer reviewers treat it as separate supporting data demonstrating specificity of DKK3 effects. Both find the control experiments acceptable.

Strong agreement on memory rescue (C106-C110). Both evaluations affirm DKK3 knockdown restores memory function in AD mice. OpenEval notes the early probe showed less robust rescue, suggesting time-dependent effects. Peer reviewers emphasize this as compelling evidence without noting temporal variations.

Both address behavioral controls (C105). OpenEval includes this within memory rescue evaluation (R9), while peer reviewers treat it separately as demonstrating specificity to memory rather than general behavioral changes. Both find it supportive.
Perfect agreement on background literature (C1, C23-C24). Both evaluations accept these as established prior findings providing context for the study. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Both address background literature (C10-C22). OpenEval groups these as established context (R11), while peer reviewers include them with other background claims and discussion points (R14). Both accept these as valid scientific background without question.

Complete agreement on DKK3 cellular localization (C35-C39). Both evaluations accept the characterization data showing DKK3 expression in excitatory neurons. OpenEval notes this is primarily descriptive; peer reviewers accept it as established characterization.

Both address therapeutic implications (C111). OpenEval notes this is reasonable inference but speculative, requiring additional validation for human translation. Peer reviewers view this positively as an implication of the work supporting Wnt pathway targeting. Both find it supported but recognize it as forward-looking.

Both address discussion/interpretation claims (C118, C120-C122). OpenEval finds these reasonable interpretations (R14), while peer reviewers accept them as valid synthesis of findings (R17). Both evaluations support these interpretive claims as consistent with the data.

Both address speculative discussion points. OpenEval includes C117 (mitochondrial hypothesis) in R14 as clearly presented speculation. Peer reviewers include C117 in R16 as future directions viewed positively. Both accept these as appropriate speculation.

Both address background and discussion claims. OpenEval's R14 covers C112-C122 as contextualization and interpretation. Peer reviewers' R14 covers overlapping background claims (C10-C22, C52, C112-C116, C119) as accepted foundational concepts. Both find these supported.

Both address negative control for cLTP (C55). OpenEval includes this within NMDAR regulation evaluation (R3) as part of the mechanistic evidence. Peer reviewers treat it separately (R15) as supporting specificity of cLTD effects. Both find it acceptable.

Minimal overlap on C52 (NMDAR activation context). OpenEval includes this as part of mechanistic link evaluation (R3). Peer reviewers include it with background literature (R14) as accepted foundational concept. Both support the claim.
